title: Windows: Embedding causes Game Bar to record embed container and not gameplay
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible since 4.4 (when game embedding was first introduced). ### System information Godot v4.7.dev (4cc119051) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7700) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.91 GiB memory ### Issue description When a scene is run from the editor with embedding enabled, popout or not, the window that (Windows) Game Bar elects to record is unfortunately the embed container, and not the game itself. ### In `4.4` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/069bedc5-434a-45ba-b16a-dcad42c35ba8 ### In `4.5` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8b30ac0-a361-46fb-b96b-1e600fb1e39e ### In `4.6`, `master` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6dbaf01-5755-48d6-bcfb-c4c3f3e456f3 ### `master`, with embedding disabled https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c05a2aa-1ab5-4b33-a63d-0913504c61f6 Screenshots, however, capture correctly. I'm reporting this for the following reasons: 1. This is likely the default hardware-agnostic tool used to screen record on Windows. 2. In case another platform is experiencing something similar. 3. In case it is within our remit to fix, rather than Microsoft's. I was on single-window mode in Windows until recently, however, so I did not have access to embedding, and would have to ask any other Game Bar users if this is a new problem that has suddenly affected all versions of Godot. ### Steps to reproduce Open any project with a scene containing a 3D camera and a WorldEnvironment. Ensure that embedding is enabled in the Game tab. Run the game and try to record it with Game Bar. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
